items.rationale: The frame sustained theft damage; §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9 allow a pre-loss-equivalent replacement. The €229 gross estimate is reduced rateably to €142.06 under the shared €500 mobility limit (§4.2.2).
The brakes sustained theft damage, so equivalent replacements are covered under §§7.1.7(b) and 7.1.9. The €140 gross estimate is reduced to €86.85 under §4.2.2.
Under §§4.2.3 and 7.1.5, a tracker must itself be affected. The original AirTag located the bike, and no theft damage to or loss of the tracker is established.
Routine servicing is excluded by §3.1.6, and §7.1.5 separately excludes work on the unaffected second bicycle.
Sections 3.1.7 and 4.2.3 exclude supplementary equipment unless it replaces equipment that was itself taken or damaged. No such loss is documented.

Section 7.1.7(f) covers necessary repair freight, provided it relates to the damaged bike or its replacement parts rather than the extra purchases. If allocated to the covered repair, €26 gross becomes €16.13 under §4.2.2.

Sections 7.1.8(f)–(g) and 7.1.10 require a necessary, nonduplicate attendance attributable to covered work; this generic charge does not establish one. If supported at €77 gross, its estimated rateable share would be about €43.60.
Fitting the replacement frame and brakes is part of the repair under §7.1.7(c), unlike fitting new accessories. The €113 gross allowance is reduced to €70.10 under §4.2.2.

Section 7.1.7(e) covers consumables used in the repair, but this generic entry does not distinguish them from materials for the other work as §7.1.10 requires. A supported €7 gross charge would yield about €4.31 after proration.

Section 7.1.7(d) allows apprentice time, but §7.1.10 requires it to be tied to the theft repair and not already included in assembly. If established at €55 gross, its rateable share would be about €31.94.

Sections 7.1.7(d) and 7.1.8(g) cover necessary repair time not already billed as assembly; this entry does not identify separate work. A distinct €39 gross hour would yield about €23.08 after proration.
Section 5.2.2(a) expressly covers the attendance needed to release the bike. A €32 gross allowance, consistent with the comparable recovery, is reduced to €19.85 under §4.2.2.
Section 5.2.2(b) covers cutting and removing the lock to release the recovered bicycle. The €108 gross estimate for the full line is reduced to €67.00 under §4.2.2.

A further attendance can qualify under §5.2.2(a), but §§7.1.8(f) and 7.1.10 require evidence it was necessary; the claim does not explain why the locksmith had to return. If substantiated at €30 gross, it would yield about €17.94 after proration.

items.description: Mandatory yard storage and release fee
items.rationale: The yard required payment before releasing the bicycle, so §5.2.2(c) covers the fee. The €100 plus 19% VAT is €119 gross; the separate €1,000 recovery cap does not bind, but §4.2.2 reduces the fee rateably to €73.82.
Sections 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d) exclude claim-processing fees. This charge is separate from the yard's mandatory release fee.

Section 5.2.2(b) allows all labour grades on lock release, but §§7.1.8(g) and 7.1.10 require separately incurred work rather than labour already billed in the cutting line. If established at €55 gross, the estimated share is €31.94.

Section 5.2.2(b) covers skilled release labour to the extent it is not duplicated in the cutting charge, consistent with the comparable recovery case. The €39 gross estimate is reduced to €24.19 under §4.2.2.
